newsitem.title: USA: SEC drops probe of central California bond deal.
newsitem.headline: SEC drops probe of central California bond deal.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has dropped its probe of a central California bond deal, ending a federal inquiry initiated by state Treasurer Matt Fong, documents showed.

The SEC told the Sierra Central Valley Public Financing Authority in a letter that its investigation "has been terminated and that, at this time, no enforcement action has been recommended to the commission."
The authority issued nearly $17 million of notes in December 1995 to buy land for a golf course project, a casino and for other purposes. An Indian tribe took part in the deal.

Earlier this year the SEC subpoenaed documents about the notes, which were issued by the authority and underwritten by San Francisco-based Pacific Genesis Group Inc. The SEC also interviewed officials involved in the bond deal.

The SEC informed the Sierra Central Valley Public Financing Authority that it was no longer a target in a two-page letter, dated June 16, to the authority's lawyer, George Forman of San Rafael, California.
Forman was not available to comment.
SEC officials declined to comment on the letter.
The SEC launched its probe of the Sierra Central Valley deal after Treasurer Fong called for the agency to investigate several bond deals underwritten by Pacific Genesis Group.

In the deals, Fong alleged that illegal payments of bond proceeds were made and that bond proceeds were used to retire private debts. The bonds were issued under the state's so-called Marks-Roos Local Bond Pooling Act, which allows local governments and agencies to form joint-power authorities to finance capital projects.
Pacific Genesis Group was not immediately available to comment on the latest development. In the past, the firm has denied wrongdoing.
In May, California's Department of Corporations -- the state's securities regulator -- said it launched its own investigation of deals underwritten by Pacific Genesis.
